Grade: SNE  /  visual-impairment / Grade 10

Topic 2.1: Oral Literature 2.1.1 Oral Narratives: Introduction
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 4

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Oral Literature 2.1.1 Oral Narratives: Introduction, part of ORAL NARRATIVES: INTRODUCTION Strand Sub Strand Specific Learning Outcomes Sugge in SNE  /  visual-impairment / Grade 10 LITERATURE IN ENGLISH FOR LEARNERS WITH VISUAL IMPAIRMENT JUNE.

Key inquiry question: Why is it important to study oral narratives?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Oral Literature 2.1.1 Oral Narratives: Introduction together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
● Communication and collaboration: This is enhanced as the learner speaks engagingly when narrating an oral

narrative to the class for peer review.

● Critical thinking and problem solving: This is advanced when the learner explores the functions of oral narratives and

identifies the features of oral narratives.

13

Values:
● Social justice: This is developed as the learner accords peers equal opportunities when teaming up to collect various

oral narratives from different communities and organise in a class portfolio.

● Peace: This is fostered as the learner harmoniously works with others to search online and offline for the types or

genres of oral narratives and make notes.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs):

Learner support programmes: This is fostered as the learner builds on their learning and research to collect oral narratives

from communities.
